payload.summary: The review-state page renders 1.73 MB of HTML and no gate watches it
payload.detail: /mockups/development/review-state lists all committed review records unpaginated - measured at 1.73 MB of served HTML for 454 records, and the corpus grows with every merge. The no-pagination choice is deliberate and correct: it is what makes the list unable to disagree with its own count, and both alternatives are worse - pagination needs a client boundary, which reintroduces the Server/Client trap this phase exists to avoid, and capping means the page hides records from its own total. But nothing measures the cost. check:bundle-budget weighs client JavaScript and these pages ship none, so the payload can grow indefinitely unnoticed. A future option worth considering is collapsible grouping by year as presentation chrome only, never filtering.
